Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with active participation of MoSPI's field offices across various States and Union Territories as well as the subordinate offices, attached and autonomous offices spread across the country, with notable achievements.
During the campaign, cleanliness drives and other related activities as mandated were organized. The progress of the campaign was regularly monitored by the Secretary, MoSPI and achievements were uploaded on a day-to-day basis on the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) Portal.
Key Achievements of Special Campaign 6.0
(i) Disposal of Pending Matters: The Ministry disposed of 48 Public Grievances and 9 Public Grievance Appeals. Efforts were also undertaken to address and expedite references received from Members of Parliament (MPs) and matters relating to Parliamentary Assurances.
(ii) Efficient File Management: A total of 718 physical files were reviewed, of which 433 files were weeded out. Additionally, 1,607 e-files were reviewed and 1,522 e-files were closed, contributing to improved records management and administrative efficiency.
(iii) Space Management: A total of 1,982 sq. ft. of office space was freed through effective space-management initiatives.
(iv) Revenue Generation: Disposal of e-waste and scrap generated revenue of ₹3,69,819, promoting better utilisation of resources.
(v) Cleanliness and Environmental Improvement: 114 Cleanliness drives were conducted, promoting workplace hygiene and environmental sustainability.
(vi) Plantation drives were conducted to promote clean and green spaces in office premises.
(vii) Felicitation ceremony to recognize and appreciate the housekeeping staff for their hard work, dedication and invaluable contribution towards maintaining a clean, hygienic and well-organised workplace.
• 'Waste to Art' campaigns were conducted in the Field offices to promote reuse and recycling initiatives.
Special One-Day Event
As part of the campaign, MoSPI organised a dedicated One-Day Cleanliness Drive on 7th October 2026 across the Ministry and its attached and subordinate offices. Activities included cleanliness and plantation drives, waste segregation, e-waste management and space optimisation. The Field Operations Division (FOD) conducted cleanliness activities at around 53 sites across the country, while other offices undertook similar initiatives at their respective locations.
The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to cleanliness, efficient administration, environmental sustainability and the timely disposal of pending matters.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with active participation of MoSPI's field offices across various States and Union Territories as well as the subordinate offices, attached and autonomous offices spread across the country, with notable achievements. During the campaign, cleanliness drives and other related activities as mandated were organized. The progress of the campaign was regularly monitored by the Secretary, MoSPI and achievements were uploaded on a day-to-day basis on the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) Portal.

Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin July-September 2026
articles.full_content:
LFPR and WPR improved in both rural and urban areas Rural UR declined Gain in employment in agriculture sector in rural areas
• The overall LFPR for persons (15+ years) reported an increase to 55.5% in July-September, 2026 compared to 54.6% in the previous quarter.
• Rural LFPR (15+ years) recorded at 58.1%, an increase of 0.9 percentage points compared with same period of last year.
• Overall WPR (15+ years) stood at 52.7% during July-September, 2026, registering an increase of 1.0 percentage point over the previous quarter.
• Rural WPR increased by 1.4 percentage points quarter-on-quarter to 55.6% during July-September, 2026.
• The share of regular wage/ salaried employment in urban areas reported an increase of 0.3 percentage points to 49.6% compared to the previous quarter.
• During July-September, 2026 the share of self-employed in rural areas increased by 1.3 percentage points to 62.7% compared with last quarter.
• Rural agricultural employment increased by 3.8 percentage points over the quarter to 56.7% during July-September, 2026 .
• Rural UR declined to 4.3% during July-September, 2026 from 4.8% in the previous quarter.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives:
• To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS).

Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Special Campaign 6 focused on institutionalising Swachhata, improving office management and reducing pendency
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has successfully concluded the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM 6). The campaign was undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026.
The campaign focused on institutionalising Swachhata, improving office management and reducing pendency across the Ministry, its attached organisations, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
During the implementation phase, the Ministry undertook various activities aimed at improving cleanliness and workplace management. Special emphasis was placed on the identification, collection, segregation and disposal of electronic waste (e-waste), ensuring better utilisation of available office space and promoting environmentally responsible waste management practices.
The Ministry made concerted efforts towards achieving the targets set under the campaign, with maximum targets successfully accomplished across the identified areas. Regular reviews and inspections of office sections were also undertaken to assess cleanliness, proper maintenance of official spaces and progress in the disposal of files and other pending matters. Officers and staff actively participated in the campaign, contributing towards maintaining clean and organised workplaces and improving administrative efficiency.
The campaign also witnessed active participation from the Ministry’s Autonomous Bodies and PSUs, ensuring a coordinated approach towards achieving the objectives.
With the successful conclusion of the implementation phase, MNRE reiterates its commitment to sustaining the achievements of the campaign through regular cleanliness drives, efficient file management, responsible e-waste disposal and a culture of accountability and timely disposal of pending matters.
articles.summary: Special Campaign 6 focused on institutionalising Swachhata, improving office management and reducing pendency The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has successfully concluded the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM 6). The campaign was undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026. The campaign focused on institutionalising Swachhata, improving office management and reducing pendency across the Ministry, its attached organisations, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
